channel.title: A new SCP I'm working on
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "A new SCP I'm working on" - I realize this is a bit similar to Scp 682 and others, but I'm trying to make it as original as possible

item.title: Re: A new SCP I'm working on
item.content:encoded:
My new idea is that they're using him to test antidotes for poisons and diseases.

I don't know how to have a narrative in an SCP file. I'd compare it to describing a character's personality. You don't tell his entire story, only the bits that have shaped him in major ways.

As for the last question, it's the same as the second one. I'd know how to make him loveable if I was writing a story and I could show his personality through action and dialogue, but in an SCP file… Maybe I should stick in some more interview logs.

item.title: Re: A new SCP I'm working on
item.content:encoded:
Ideas like this generally have the same flaw, that they seem like misery for the sake of misery. You've crafted a story about a kid getting tortured by the Foundation, but to what end? I'm not really getting a sense for a character arc or a real… narrative thread that's being followed and delivered upon.

I guess generally you should ask what the point of all this misery is. What sort of emotions are you attempting to evoke from your audience, and how do you plan to endear this main character to them?

item.title: Re: A new SCP I'm working on
item.content:encoded: Good point. Maybe they try a couple of normal tests, realize there's no keeping him down long, and then test all kinds of poisons and diseases without known cures to find said cures.

item.title: Re: A new SCP I'm working on
item.content:encoded:
Hi there, I am not an official critter but let me share some thoughts here.

First off, you must remember that the Foundation is cold, not cruel. Why would they continue testing on the boy when the effects of his anomalous abilities are clear from the beginning? They would hardly go past one or two tests and once they were sure this is a child who happens to return from the dead they would keep him in custody in a somewhat nice cell and call it a day. That's what was done to 053 herself.

If the bulk of your narrative was just testing logs then you don't really have a narrative yet. Few people would be interested in reading about a child being tortured. The narrative needs a progression, an arc, maybe it can be the boy telling his life, or the efforts of a researcher to find the boy's family or what is left of them. The readers must feel something when reading your article, you must define what it is you want them to feel and then write around it. If your goal is to make us feel sorry for the boy I still suggest approaching it on a less gratuitously violent way.

Good luck on your writing!

item.title: A new SCP I'm working on
item.content:encoded:
Scp 5091 is a boy who died in 1909 but came back to life in his coffin. He suffocated from lack of air, then came back. This went on until the cemetery he was buried in was dug up and he was taken in by the foundation, who now use him as to test possible cures to different poisons/diseases.

I call him Ressurection Teddy, as a nod to the legend of Resurrection Mary. Does that count as plagiarism?

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This kid isn't any stronger than a normal child, and he can be killed just the same, but nothing will keep him down permanently, even if it takes months for him to recover.

Central Narrative: The different test the foundation tests the foundation conducted on him. After being killed and coming back to life a few times, they decide to use him as a lab rat to develop cures to poisons and diseases that are currently without cures.

+ show block
– hide block

The things they've tested on him are AIDS/HIV, different types of prions, ricin, amatoxin, tetrodotoxin, and even a few anomalous diseases and poisons.

The kid was already traumatized from being buried for so long, and these tests only made things worse.

During an interview, he asks where his parents are. The doctor tells him they're likely dead, and he has a panic attack and hasn't talked since. Testing was suspended, and the poor thing is being given counseling.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: He can't be killed permanently, at least not in any way that the foundation has discovered.

Additional Notes: The 5091 number is a placeholder, I'll give it another number when I post it to the mainsite.
